plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own bid), there's no incentive to shade the bid up or down—overbidding risks winning at a loss, underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $21, the optimal action is to bid exactly $21, ensuring I maximize expected profit given the mechanism's incentive structure.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding my actual value of $7 maximizes my expected profit—I won't overpay if I win, and I won't miss profitable opportunities by underbidding. There's no benefit to shading my bid up or down in this format, regardless of what other bidders do. I'll bid exactly my value.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the highest competing bid, and you pay only the second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you're the highest). Bidding above value risks overpaying; bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions. With no prior history to adjust for, I'll bid exactly my value of $34 to maximize expected profit.
